items.name: Longbow
items.intent: The ranger's baseline: reliable at six hexes, and one hex further if you are willing to pay double.

items.name: Shortbow
items.intent: Short in the draw and short in the range, but the only bow that will shoot for free.

items.name: Elfbow
items.intent: It does not hit harder than a longbow; it simply does not miss, and when it must, it misses twice at once.

items.name: Barbarian Bow
items.intent: A bow built by someone who wanted it to be an axe; it hits like one and aims like one too.

items.name: Javelin
items.intent: The only tier-1 weapon that is genuinely both — throw it at four hexes or keep it and stab.

items.name: Longsword
items.intent: The reference weapon: cheap-and-reliable or expensive-and-heavy, and nothing else to think about.
items.source: settled content | 2026-09-23 V2 R1: +5 Block (swords +5 one-handed, +10 two-handed; knives and daggers +5; Block only) — V2-SHIELDS-AND-WEAPONS-2026-09-20.md, ruled 2026-09-20

items.name: Halberd
items.intent: Two hands, two hexes of consequence: shove one enemy off you, or catch three of them at once.

items.name: Fire Staff
items.intent: Burn one thing every turn, or burn seven hexes of ground once.

items.name: Frost Staff
items.intent: Frost cancels burn and amplifies the next physical hit, so this staff is a setup tool wearing a weapon's clothes.

items.name: Earth Staff
items.intent: The only staff whose power points the other way — it protects an ally instead of painting the ground.

items.name: Lightning Staff
items.intent: The longest reach and the hardest hit of any staff, and it will miss more than any of them.

items.name: Force Staff
items.intent: One attack and no power at all — but the blast scales on Magic as well as Precision, so the staff pays a mage back for every point of it.
items.source: settled content | 2026-09-02: Force Blast re-ruled to precision + half Magic at 1 stamina.

items.name: Holy Symbol
items.intent: A hand's worth of god: it hurts the walking dead and mends the walking living.
items.source: settled content | 2026-09-02b workbook: tagged staff, which it is not. It is a holy symbol.

items.name: Priest Chain
items.intent: A censer on a length of chain — it swings at one enemy and blesses everyone behind it.
items.source: settled content | 2026-09-02b workbook: joins the CHAIN set.

items.name: Pile of Rocks
items.intent: It is rocks. You throw them. They are free and they are accurate and they do almost nothing.

items.name: Pitchfork
items.intent: Two hands and a farm tool's balance; it is a real damage point and a real apology.

items.name: Club
items.intent: A length of wood with the bark still on it, and it takes the strength out of whatever it lands on.

items.name: Dagger
items.intent: Fast, free and barely lethal — you stab with it mostly to keep your guard up.
items.source: settled content | 2026-09-23 V2 R1: +5 Block (swords +5 one-handed, +10 two-handed; knives and daggers +5; Block only) — V2-SHIELDS-AND-WEAPONS-2026-09-20.md, ruled 2026-09-20

items.name: Basic Armor
items.intent: One point of Health and not one word of drawback — the floor everything else is measured against.
items.source: settled content | 2026-08-27: slots 0 — tier-0 armor never costs an item slot (dedicated armor slot, one armor per unit). startClasses is the start-draw pool; USE is universal across classes.

items.name: Flowing Cloak
items.intent: It does not stop anything; it just makes you slightly harder to be sure about.
items.source: settled content | 2026-08-27: slots 0 — tier-0 armor never costs an item slot (dedicated armor slot, one armor per unit). startClasses is the start-draw pool; USE is universal across classes.

items.name: Nice Robes
items.intent: Good cloth, well cut, and the only protection it offers is that nobody wants to ruin it.
items.source: settled content | 2026-08-27: slots 0 — tier-0 armor never costs an item slot (dedicated armor slot, one armor per unit). startClasses is the start-draw pool; USE is universal across classes.

items.name: Ragged Hides
items.intent: Twice the Health of basic armour, and it takes a point of stamina every fight to wear.
items.source: settled content | 2026-08-27: slots 0 — tier-0 armor never costs an item slot (dedicated armor slot, one armor per unit). startClasses is the start-draw pool; USE is universal across classes.

items.name: Rusted Plate
items.intent: One point of Armor for four separate miseries — this is the item the armoursmith exists to replace.
items.source: settled content | 2026-08-27: slots 0 — tier-0 armor never costs an item slot (dedicated armor slot, one armor per unit). startClasses is the start-draw pool; USE is universal across classes.

items.name: Destroyed Mail
items.intent: Four Health is a lot at tier 0, and twenty Accuracy is what four Health costs when the mail is in pieces.
items.source: settled content | 2026-08-27: slots 0 — tier-0 armor never costs an item slot (dedicated armor slot, one armor per unit). startClasses is the start-draw pool; USE is universal across classes.

items.name: Barbarian Hide
items.intent: Light armour that buys stamina and luck instead of Health, with nothing given back.

items.name: Studded Leather
items.intent: Two Health, clean, no cost — the light band's honest baseline.

items.name: Heavy Leather
items.intent: The heaviest thing in the light band: it trades the band's own Dodge and stamina for Health.

items.name: Heavy Chain
items.intent: A point of Armor for a hex of Movement, and no other conversation.

items.name: Mismatched Armor
items.intent: Four pieces from four dead men; it covers you and it slows you and it matches nothing.

items.name: Creature Hide
items.intent: Something's skin, and whatever it was, things still seem reluctant to land a good hit on it.

items.name: Plated Armor
items.intent: The heavy band at full commitment: two Armor and four Health, and you will never dodge anything again.

items.name: Reflective Armor
items.intent: The only tier-1 armour that answers magic, and it costs three hexes of Movement to wear.

items.name: Soaked Plate
items.intent: Heavy plate with no penalty at all, which is the strangest thing in the band.

items.name: Fire Gauntlet
items.intent: The one mage weapon that wants you in reach. Strength swings it and Magic is what actually burns.
items.source: Ruled 2026-09-02b, dictated: the priest and mage ladder above tier 3, and the sets it hangs on.

items.name: Staff of Summoning
items.intent: It calls one thing up and it is unusually good at putting other people's things back down.
items.source: Ruled 2026-09-02b, dictated: the priest and mage ladder above tier 3, and the sets it hangs on.

items.name: Staff of the Magi
items.intent: The staff is the smaller half. What it really is, is a reason to fill every slot you own with rings.
items.source: Ruled 2026-09-02b, dictated: the priest and mage ladder above tier 3, and the sets it hangs on.
items.setBonusText: +1 Magic for every RING you are wearing.

items.name: Staff of the Destroyer
items.intent: Nothing it kills gets to be raised, walked past, or mourned. There is no corpse.
items.source: Ruled 2026-09-02b, dictated: the priest and mage ladder above tier 3, and the sets it hangs on.
items.setBonusText: +1 damage for every DESTROYER item you carry.

items.name: Staff of the Ultimate Destroyer
items.intent: The last staff. It doubles the stat it scales on and then scales on it.
items.source: Ruled 2026-09-02b, dictated: the priest and mage ladder above tier 3, and the sets it hangs on.
items.setBonusText: +1 damage for every DESTROYER item you carry.

items.name: Chains of the Wrathful
items.intent: Both hands, swung wide. It is the only priest weapon that does not care which one of them it hits.
items.source: Ruled 2026-09-02b, dictated: the priest and mage ladder above tier 3, and the sets it hangs on.
items.setBonusText: +1 Precision for every CHAIN item you carry.

items.name: Benevolent Rod
items.intent: One good heal on a clock and one small one you can spend every single Turn.
items.source: Ruled 2026-09-02b, dictated: the priest and mage ladder above tier 3, and the sets it hangs on.

items.name: Book of Karma
items.intent: The ledger is kept whether or not you read it aloud. Reading it aloud is how someone else gets paid.
items.source: Ruled 2026-09-02b, dictated: the priest and mage ladder above tier 3, and the sets it hangs on.
items.setBonusText: +1 Resist for every BOOK you carry.

items.name: Rod of Imprisonment
items.intent: It does not hurt anything. It takes one thing off the board for a Turn -- theirs, or, when it has to be, yours.
items.source: Ruled 2026-09-02b, dictated: the priest and mage ladder above tier 3, and the sets it hangs on.

items.name: Kite Shield
items.intent: Long and pointed, built for the melee line: +20 against blades, little against arrows.

items.name: Round Shield
items.intent: Even on every side and cheap to use.

items.name: Tower Shield
items.intent: Better at everything, paid for in Dodge and Stamina.
items.source: V2-SHIELDS-AND-WEAPONS-2026-09-20.md, ruled 2026-09-20; fifth pass: re-authors item.tower-shield in place

attacks.name: Shot
attacks.intent: The cheap, repeatable shot the whole class is built around.

attacks.name: Long Shot
attacks.intent: One more hex and one more point of damage, for twice the stamina.

attacks.name: Short Shot
attacks.intent: Closer in than a longbow wants to be, and steadier for it.

attacks.name: Quick Shot
attacks.intent: Costs nothing, so it is what you do on the turn you have nothing left.

attacks.name: Elf Shot
attacks.intent: Fifteen Accuracy instead of a damage point — reliability as the whole payload.
attacks.source: settled content | 2026-08-27 review: damage 0 -> -1, gains onHit: +1 Precision (stacking, for the Battle).

attacks.name: Double Shot
attacks.intent: Two weak arrows in the time of one good one; it is a spread, not an upgrade.

attacks.name: Power Shot

triggers.effect: push the target 1 hex directly away from you

attacks.intent: The hardest-hitting tier-1 shot, paid for in Accuracy and a hex of shove.

attacks.name: Crippling Shot
attacks.intent: Trades a damage point for two Weak — the shot you open a big enemy with.

attacks.name: Throw
attacks.intent: Ranged damage on a one-handed weapon, and the Accuracy is what it costs.

attacks.name: Stab
attacks.intent: Free, and better than a punch — the reason you keep hold of it.
attacks.source: settled content | 2026-08-27 review: crit 3 -> 6. | 2026-09-02, from the weapon outlier review: damage lowered by 1 — a 0-stamina attack does not also carry positive damage. Ruled.

attacks.name: Slash
attacks.intent: One stamina, one damage; the honest option.

attacks.name: Stab
attacks.intent: Twice the stamina for more damage, more Accuracy and more Crit — the committed swing.

attacks.name: Hack

triggers.effect: push the target 1 hex directly away from you

attacks.intent: Strong, cheap, and it makes room — the warrior's default halberd swing.

attacks.name: Cleave
attacks.targets: an adjacent hex and the two hexes adjacent to both you and it
attacks.description: A hex-targeted burst affecting all units in the authored three-hex arc, dealing Strength + 1 physical damage. Standard V2 burst shielding and attenuation apply. It is not an attack.
attacks.intent: Three hexes in one swing, at the price of never critting.
attacks.source: settled content | V2 migration 2026-09-16 (provisional): preserve authored shape, costs, range and magnitude; explicit all-units burst, no attack hooks or rolls. Earlier description: An area attack across a three-hex arc. It does not roll to hit, so it cannot crit.

attacks.name: Fire Blast
attacks.intent: The mage's repeatable magic attack, with a burn stack riding on it.

attacks.name: Frost Blast
attacks.intent: Same shape as Fire Blast, but the stack it leaves makes your melee hit harder.

attacks.name: Earth Blast

triggers.effect: push the target 1 hex directly away from you

attacks.intent: Shortest range of the staves, and the only one that moves the target.

attacks.name: Bolt
attacks.intent: Three damage at five hexes, bought with the largest Accuracy penalty at the tier.

attacks.name: Force Blast
attacks.description: Damage equals your Precision plus the party's Magic.
attacks.intent: Deliberately the only tier-1 weapon with one attack; the double scaling is what it bought.
attacks.source: settled content | RE-RULED 2026-09-02, verbatim: 'Change it to precision +1/2, magic, and stamina 1.' So: precision plus HALF the attacker's Magic, magic damage, one stamina — was precision+0 for two stamina, the worst damage-per-stamina in tier 1. Uses the same halfStatBonus field as the Ancient Tome's Read the Page (2026-08-27); the half rounds nearest, 0.5 up, per the standing rounding ruling, and the field is a named engine gap on both attacks.

attacks.name: Wrath
attacks.intent: True damage ignores mitigation entirely, and against undead it is two points better again.

attacks.name: Smite
attacks.intent: A point better than Wrath, with no slayer line and no Accuracy bonus.

attacks.name: Throw
attacks.intent: Zero stamina and +10 Accuracy against a damage point of negative one.

attacks.name: Jab
attacks.intent: Tier-1 damage on a tier-0 weapon, paid for with both hands and some Accuracy.

attacks.name: Swing
attacks.intent: No damage bonus; the Weak stack is the whole weapon.

attacks.name: Stab
attacks.intent: It pays you a point of protection every time you swing, whether or not you connect.

attacks.name: Fire Punch

triggers.effect: apply Burn equal to half your Magic, rounded nearest, 0.5 up

attacks.description: Damage equals your Strength, dealt as magic, and it leaves half your Magic burning on them.
attacks.source: Ruled 2026-09-02b, dictated: the priest and mage ladder above tier 3, and the sets it hangs on.

attacks.name: Unbinding
attacks.description: Damage equals your Precision plus half the party's Magic, and you are 15 Accuracy better against anything summoned.
attacks.source: Ruled 2026-09-02b, dictated: the priest and mage ladder above tier 3, and the sets it hangs on.

attacks.name: Ruin
attacks.description: Damage equals your Precision plus twice the party's Magic. Anything it kills leaves nothing behind.
attacks.source: Ruled 2026-09-02b, dictated: the priest and mage ladder above tier 3, and the sets it hangs on.

attacks.name: Sundering
attacks.description: The same damage two hexes further out, and it takes two Activations off whatever survives it.
attacks.source: Ruled 2026-09-02b, dictated: the priest and mage ladder above tier 3, and the sets it hangs on.

attacks.name: Annihilation
attacks.description: Damage equals twice your Precision plus twice the party's Magic. Once every five Turns, and it costs most of a Turn's Stamina.
attacks.source: Ruled 2026-09-02b, dictated: the priest and mage ladder above tier 3, and the sets it hangs on.

attacks.name: Wrathful Sweep
attacks.description: Damage equals 1 plus the party's Spirit, to everything within 3 hexes. As an area effect it does not roll and cannot crit.
attacks.source: Ruled 2026-09-02b, dictated: the priest and mage ladder above tier 3, and the sets it hangs on. | The dictated line is "1+spirit" with no Precision term, which makes this the ONLY attack in the codex still scaling on Spirit alone -- every other priest attack was moved to precision + 1/2 spirit in the same pass. Kept as dictated; it is the two-handed area weapon, so paying entirely in the party stat is the trade.

powers.name: Flame Burst
powers.targets: a hex within 4 hexes and every hex adjacent to it
powers.description: Deal magic damage equal to your Magic to every unit in the blast, and those seven hexes become burning. It does not roll to hit, so it cannot crit, and allies caught in it burn too.
powers.source: settled content | 2026-08-19: power.fire-master.fireball owns "Fireball" — two powers with one name is the worst of the collisions. The staff grants the smaller baseline version. | 2026-08-20: ground layers are PERSISTENT and carry no number and no clock. A hex is burning or it is not. One layer per hex; applying a different one replaces it. See rule.ground-layers. | 2026-10-04 (engine fix.starting-kit-powers; reported 2026-10-03, engine DECISIONS.md "reported: the priest's Holy Texts has no heal in battle"): the blast is declared as a V2 burst profile, the Lightning Staff's Storm shape (radius 1, every unit, one Magic packet) — the description is unchanged. The ground it leaves is not in the profile: a burst paints no ground yet (engine capability.burst-paints-ground), and the pack names that gap on the row. | 2026-10-04 (engine capability.burst-paints-ground): the profile now names the ground the blast leaves — burst.paints, the layer — so “those seven hexes become burning” reaches the engine and the gap is gone. The ground is painted after the blast’s damage, and every unit standing on the seven hexes meets it as ground always meets a unit it is painted under.
powers.intent: The blast is the smaller half; the burning ground it leaves is the real payload.

powers.name: Earth Shield
powers.description: The target ally gains 3 + Magic Protection.
powers.source: settled content
powers.intent: Protection scaled off the party's Magic — a mage keeping the front line standing.

powers.name: Storm
powers.targets: a hex within 4 hexes and every hex adjacent to it
powers.description: A hex-targeted burst affecting all units in the centre hex and its six neighbours, dealing Magic + 1 magic damage. Standard V2 burst shielding and attenuation apply. It is not an attack.
powers.source: settled content | V2 migration 2026-09-16 (provisional): preserve authored shape, costs, range and magnitude; explicit all-units burst, no attack hooks or rolls. Earlier description: Deal magic damage equal to your Magic + 1 to every unit in the blast. It does not roll to hit, so it cannot crit.
powers.intent: Pure damage where the other staves leave terrain — one more point, nothing lingering.

powers.name: Heal
powers.description: Heal the target for 1 + 2 x Spirit.
powers.source: settled content
powers.intent: Doubled Spirit scaling is what makes a priest worth the slot.

powers.name: Benediction
powers.description: Heal every ally within 6 hexes for 2 + half your Spirit, rounded nearest, 0.5 up (aligned 2026-08-25 — the old 'rounded down' is superseded by the half-stat rounding ruling).
powers.source: settled content | 2026-08-20 sweep: "hero" in a mechanical sentence — the word everywhere else is "ally", and an ally shape already exists. Same effect, one vocabulary.
powers.intent: Party-wide healing at half the scaling — breadth instead of depth.

powers.name: Ignite
powers.targets: a hex within 4 hexes and every hex adjacent to it
powers.description: The target hex and every hex adjacent to it become burning. It does not roll to hit, so it cannot crit.
powers.source: settled content | 2026-08-20: ground layers are PERSISTENT and carry no number and no clock. A hex is burning or it is not. One layer per hex; applying a different one replaces it. See rule.ground-layers.
powers.intent: The terrain half of the fire enchant, on a long enough cooldown to be a decision.

powers.name: Light It
powers.description: Once per Battle, free: set a forest hex within 1 alight — the hex gains the burning ground layer.
powers.intent: The cheap answer to a forest, and the reason a torch is not just a lamp.
powers.source: Authored 2026-09-02: the Torch's option was written in its description only, so the merged R37 (trinket-is-a-stat-stick) correctly read the item as pure stats. The option was always the design — this expresses it in data, where the rule can see it.

powers.name: Mercy
powers.description: Heal the target for 2 + half your Spirit.
powers.source: 2026-09-02b workbook: Mercy was written as an ATTACK aimed at an ally, which is not a thing the engine can be asked to do. It is a power. Ruled 2026-09-02b, dictated: the priest and mage ladder above tier 3, and the sets it hangs on.
powers.intent: The same book either way -- you are choosing which of two people it is aimed at.

powers.name: Salvation
powers.description: Heal the target for 4 + your Spirit.
powers.source: 2026-09-02b workbook: was an attack aimed at an ally; rewritten as a power, healing 4 + Spirit. Ruled 2026-09-02b, dictated: the priest and mage ladder above tier 3, and the sets it hangs on.
powers.intent: The mercy you were going to spend anyway, aimed on purpose for once.

powers.name: Stoke
powers.description: For your next 3 Activations, every hit you land applies Burn equal to half your Magic, rounded nearest, 0.5 up.
powers.source: Ruled 2026-09-02b, dictated: the priest and mage ladder above tier 3, and the sets it hangs on.
powers.intent: A mage buying three Activations of burn onto whatever else they were already doing.

powers.name: Call the Wolf
powers.targets: an empty hex adjacent to you
powers.description: Summon one Wolf on a hex adjacent to you. It is a summoned ally with its own stat block and its own AI.
powers.source: Ruled 2026-09-02b, dictated: the priest and mage ladder above tier 3, and the sets it hangs on.
powers.intent: Two Stamina and a five-Turn wait for a body that is not yours.

powers.name: Power Ward
powers.description: You gain 8 + (Magic x 2) Protection.
powers.source: Ruled 2026-09-02b, dictated: the priest and mage ladder above tier 3, and the sets it hangs on.
powers.intent: Three Turns of warning and ten of waiting, for the largest single block in the game.

powers.name: Vortex
powers.targets: a hex within 5 hexes and every hex adjacent to it
powers.description: Deal magic damage equal to Magic x 3 to every unit in the blast. It does not roll to hit, so it cannot crit. Using it lowers the party's Magic by 1 AND the enemy side's Power by 1 for the rest of the Battle.
powers.source: Ruled 2026-09-02b, dictated: the priest and mage ladder above tier 3, and the sets it hangs on.
powers.intent: It eats the magic out of the field -- yours and theirs, one point each. The blast is enormous and every spell cast after it, on either side, is smaller.

powers.name: Perfect Sight
powers.description: Until the end of your third Activation from now, your Precision is doubled (Precision added to Precision).
powers.source: Ruled 2026-09-02b, dictated: the priest and mage ladder above tier 3, and the sets it hangs on. | CONFIRMED 2026-09-03: "add precision to precision" -- the dictation's "perception" was Precision, and the effect is doubling, not a flat bonus.
powers.intent: Two Stamina to make the next three Activations count twice.

powers.name: Weight of Sin
powers.description: Every enemy within 3 hexes gains Weak equal to half your Spirit, rounded nearest, 0.5 up, and 2 Slow.
powers.source: Ruled 2026-09-02b, dictated: the priest and mage ladder above tier 3, and the sets it hangs on.
powers.intent: No damage at all -- it just makes the next three things everyone else does land harder.

powers.name: Mending Light
powers.description: Heal the target for (Spirit x 2) + 2, give it Protection equal to your Spirit, and remove Weak equal to your Spirit.
powers.source: Ruled 2026-09-02b, dictated: the priest and mage ladder above tier 3, and the sets it hangs on.
powers.intent: Three things at once, which is why it waits two Turns between castings.

powers.name: Small Mercy
powers.description: Free, 0 Stamina: heal the target for your Spirit.
powers.source: Ruled 2026-09-02b, dictated: the priest and mage ladder above tier 3, and the sets it hangs on.
powers.intent: Costs nothing and reaches seven hexes, so there is never a Turn it is wrong to use.

powers.name: Balance the Ledger
powers.description: Heal the target for 3 + half your Spirit, rounded nearest, 0.5 up, and give it 2 Karma.
powers.source: Ruled 2026-09-02b, dictated: the priest and mage ladder above tier 3, and the sets it hangs on.
powers.intent: The heal is the smaller half. Karma makes every heal after it bigger and every hit it lands harder.

powers.name: Imprison
powers.description: Until the end of its next Activation the target has +10 Armor and +10 Resist. It also gains 1 Stun and 2 Root.
powers.source: Ruled 2026-09-02b, dictated: the priest and mage ladder above tier 3, and the sets it hangs on.
powers.intent: You pay for the Stun by making it briefly very hard to kill. Use it on the thing you were never going to kill this Turn.

powers.name: Hallow
powers.description: Free: until the end of your next Activation you have +10 Armor, +10 Resist, 2 Root and -100 Accuracy.
powers.source: Ruled 2026-09-02b, dictated: the priest and mage ladder above tier 3, and the sets it hangs on.
powers.intent: You stop being a threat and you stop being a target. It is the button you press when the answer is to survive the Turn.

powers.name: Turn Aside
powers.description: Gain +10 Block and +10 Ranged Block until the end of your next Activation.
powers.intent: The cheap even guard: lift the rim and let it glance.
powers.source: V2-SHIELDS-AND-WEAPONS-2026-09-20.md, ruled 2026-09-20, fourth pass — provisional numbers, engine/SWITCHES.md shieldPowerNumbers; to be corrected from battles

powers.name: Bear Down
powers.description: Gain +5 Block, +5 Ranged Block and +1 Armor until the end of your next Activation.
powers.intent: Plant the feet behind the boss and take it.
powers.source: V2-SHIELDS-AND-WEAPONS-2026-09-20.md, ruled 2026-09-20, fourth pass — provisional numbers, engine/SWITCHES.md shieldPowerNumbers; to be corrected from battles

powers.name: Lock Shields
powers.description: Gain +15 Block and +1 Armor until the end of your next Activation.
powers.intent: The melee line's answer to the melee line.
powers.source: V2-SHIELDS-AND-WEAPONS-2026-09-20.md, ruled 2026-09-20, fourth pass — provisional numbers, engine/SWITCHES.md shieldPowerNumbers; to be corrected from battles

powers.name: Counterattack
powers.description: Gain Counterattack with +10 Accuracy until the end of your next Turn.
powers.intent: The sword answers. Until your next Turn is over, an enemy that swings at you from the next hex gets your basic attack back when its own attacks are done — free, at the free attack’s −20, less this power’s +10.
powers.source: 2026-09-28 (engine/DECISIONS.md ‘counterattack, special free attacks, the opening six, shields, custom weapons’): "Counterattack is set off by being attacked, not by being hit, blocked, or dodged." "You can counterattack once per enemy action, so if that enemy action is three attacks, all three of their attacks will resolve, and then you will get your one counterattack." "Until the end of next turn." "The counter strike is with +10 accuracy. That's the one it has. Costs 2 stamina." Ruled there: ‘The longsword’s second power: counterattack with +10 Accuracy, until the end of your next turn, 2 Stamina.’ A counterattack is a special free attack: the basic attack, no Stamina, −20 Accuracy. Row added 2026-10-04 by engine item capability.counterattack-and-fend. The Longsword keeps Stab for now: the dictation would retire its 2-Stamina attack for this power, and that is the weapon list’s to do (engine SWITCHES.md longswordKeepsStab).

powers.name: Raise Guard

enchants.intent: The weapon's own basic attack, burning: a stack of Burn and two points of fire on every hit, and nothing on a miss.
enchants.source: Custom weapon series 'Flaming', tier 3 (Armory Ledger, approved for now 2026-09-28, engine DECISIONS.md 'the Armory Ledger is approved for now'): "Basic attack, on hit: Burn 1 and 2 fire damage." Dictated V2-SHIELDS-AND-WEAPONS-2026-09-20.md 317: "Tier 3. This is a basic attack. On hit, 1 burn and 2 fire damage." A custom weapon is a series across base weapons (the Ledger's rules: Flaming Axe, Flaming Longsword, Flaming Halberd); the basic attack is the base's first attack. The tier-3 Flaming Longsword is the reward after opening battle 2 (engine DECISIONS.md 2026-09-28 'custom weapons are series across base weapons'). Tiers 4-6 are not built.
